facts: A fox has a big fluffy tail.
Foxes hear a mouse squeak from far away.
Red foxes live on more continents than any other wild dog.
ask: Can you tiptoe as quietly as a fox?
twin: grey-wolf
A fox is small with a thin pointy face; a wolf is big like a large dog.

facts: A hedgehog rolls into a prickly ball.
A hedgehog has about 6,000 spines.
Hedgehogs sleep all winter and their heart slows to 20 beats a minute.
ask: Curl up into a ball like a hedgehog!
twin: echidna
A hedgehog has short legs and a pointy nose; an echidna has a long thin beak-nose and lays eggs.

facts: Squirrels bury nuts to eat later.
Red squirrels grow tufts on their ears in winter.
Forgotten nuts grow into new trees — squirrels plant forests.
ask: Where would you hide a nut?
twin: grey-squirrel
Red squirrels are smaller, red-orange, with ear tufts; grey squirrels are bigger and grey.

facts: A badger has a black and white striped face.
Badgers dig big homes called setts.
Some badger setts are over 100 years old, used by many generations.
ask: Can you dig like a badger with your hands?

facts: Daddy deer have big antlers.
Antlers fall off every year and grow back.
Antlers are among the fastest-growing body parts — up to 2 cm a day.
ask: Make antlers with your hands!
twin: roe-deer
Red deer are big like horses; roe deer are small like a big dog.

photos.by: derivative work: Massimo Catarinella (talk) Red_deer_stag.jpg: Mehmet Karatay

facts: Baby deer have white spots.
Roe deer bark like dogs when scared.
A fawn has almost no smell, so predators walk right past it.
ask: Can you freeze still like a baby deer?

facts: Baby boars have stripes like watermelons.
Boars dig with their strong snouts.
All farm pigs come from wild boars.
ask: Snuffle like a boar looking for food!
twin: pig
A wild boar is hairy and brown with tusks; a farm pig is pink with little hair.

facts: Rabbits hop and wiggle their noses.
Rabbits thump their feet to warn friends.
A rabbit's teeth never stop growing — chewing keeps them short.
ask: Hop like a rabbit three times!
twin: hare
Rabbits are smaller with shorter ears; hares are bigger, with long black-tipped ears.

facts: Hares have very long ears.
Hares can run as fast as a car in town.
Baby hares are born with fur and open eyes, ready to run.
ask: Who is faster, you or a hare?

facts: Bears sleep all winter in a den.
Brown bears love berries, fish and honey.
A brown bear can smell food from many kilometres away.
ask: Give a big bear hug!
twin: black-bear
Brown bears have a shoulder hump; black bears have no hump and taller ears.

sound.by: NPS & MSU Acoustic Atlas / Jennifer Jerrett

video.by: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, National Conservation Training Center (USFWS/NCTC)

facts: Wolves howl to talk to their family.
Wolves live in families called packs.
Every pet dog in the world comes from wolves.
ask: Howl like a wolf!

facts: A lynx has pointy tufts on its ears.
Big furry paws work like snowshoes.
Lynx returned to the Alps after people brought them back.
ask: Walk on soft paws like a lynx.

facts: Otters swim and love fish.
Otters can close their ears and nose underwater.
Otter fur is so thick that water never touches their skin.
ask: Pretend to swim like an otter!
twin: smooth-otter
Eurasian otters live alone; smooth-coated otters live in big noisy families.

facts: Beavers build houses with sticks.
Beaver teeth are orange because they contain iron.
Beaver dams make ponds that help hundreds of other animals.
ask: What would you build with sticks?
twin: american-beaver
They look almost the same! Eurasian beavers have a narrower tail and longer nose.

facts: Marmots whistle when danger comes.
Marmots sleep for half the year.
A whole family hibernates together, snuggled to stay warm.
ask: Whistle like a marmot!

facts: Ibex climb steep mountains.
Ibex horns can grow a metre long.
Ibex climb almost straight dam walls to lick salt.
ask: Balance on one foot like an ibex on a rock!

facts: Bats fly at night.
Bats find food by listening to echoes.
This tiny bat eats around 3,000 insects in one night.
ask: Close your eyes — can you find a sound?

sound.by: XN URL: Ex :: Natura - Freies Portal zu Naturerlebnis und Umweltbildung (Environmental Education)

facts: Moles dig tunnels under the grass.
Moles have huge shovel hands.
A mole can dig 20 metres of tunnel in a day.
ask: Dig like a mole with your hands!

facts: A moose is taller than a grown-up.
Moose are great swimmers.
A moose can dive 5 metres to eat water plants.
ask: Stretch up tall like a moose!

facts: Mummy and daddy reindeer both have antlers.
Reindeer feet click when they walk.
Reindeer eyes turn from gold to blue in the dark winter.
ask: Click your tongue like reindeer feet!

facts: Sparrows hop around people.
Sparrows take baths in dust.
House sparrows have lived beside people for 10,000 years.
ask: Can you hop like a sparrow?
twin: robin
Sparrows are brown and stripy; robins have an orange chest.

facts: Robins have an orange tummy.
Robins sing even in winter.
Robins follow gardeners to grab worms they dig up.
ask: What colour is a robin's tummy?
twin: american-robin
The European robin is tiny; the American robin is a bigger thrush.

facts: Daddy blackbird is black with an orange beak.
Mummy blackbird is brown.
Blackbirds in cities sing earlier and louder than in forests.
ask: Which bird sings outside your window?

facts: It has a black stripe like a tie.
Its song sounds like "tea-cher".
Great tits can learn to open new kinds of feeders by watching friends.
ask: Sing "tea-cher, tea-cher"!
twin: blue-tit
Great tits are bigger with a black head; blue tits are smaller with a blue cap.

facts: A tiny bird with a blue hat.
Blue tits hang upside down to eat.
Parents bring up to 1,000 caterpillars a day to their chicks.
ask: Can you find something blue?

facts: Magpies are black and white.
Their black feathers shine green and blue.
Magpies recognise themselves in a mirror — very rare for birds.
ask: Make a black and white drawing!

facts: Crows are all black.
Crows are super clever puzzle solvers.
Crows remember faces of people for years.
ask: Caw like a crow!
twin: raven
Crows are smaller with a square tail; ravens are huge with a diamond tail and croak.

facts: Ravens are big black birds.
Ravens can copy sounds, even words.
Ravens do somersaults in the air just for fun.
ask: Do a roll like a raven playing!

facts: Pigeons coo and bob their heads.
Pigeons always find their way home.
Pigeons carried messages in wars and won medals.
ask: Bob your head like a pigeon!

facts: Ducks say quack!
Daddy ducks have a shiny green head.
Only mummy mallards make the loud "quack" sound.
ask: Waddle like a duck!

facts: Swans are big and white.
Baby swans are grey and fluffy.
Swan wings make a loud humming sound when they fly.
ask: Make a long swan neck with your arm!

photos.by: Feel free to use my photos, but please mention me as the author and if you want send me a message. or (rufre@lenz-nenning.at)

video.by: No machine-readable author provided. TeunSpaans assumed (based on copyright claims).

facts: Storks build nests on rooftops.
Storks clack their beaks to say hello.
Storks fly all the way to Africa for winter and back.
ask: Stand on one leg like a stork!
twin: heron
Storks are white with a red beak; herons are grey and fly with a folded neck.

facts: Herons stand very still in water.
Herons catch fish super fast.
A heron can stand still for ages, waiting for a fish to swim by.
ask: Stand still like a heron — who moves first?

facts: Kingfishers are bright blue and orange.
Kingfishers dive into water for fish.
Japan's fast trains got their shape from the kingfisher's beak.
ask: Dive like a kingfisher!

facts: Barn owls have a heart-shaped face.
Barn owls fly without a sound.
A barn owl can catch a mouse in total darkness by sound alone.
ask: Turn your head like an owl!
twin: tawny-owl
Barn owls are white with a heart face; tawny owls are brown with dark eyes.

facts: Owls say twit-twoo at night.
"Twit" is mummy, "twoo" is daddy.
Owls can turn their heads almost all the way around.
ask: Twit-twoo! Who is mummy, who is daddy?

facts: Buzzards fly in big circles.
Buzzards ride warm air to go up.
A buzzard can see a mouse from 100 metres up.
ask: Fly in circles like a buzzard!

facts: Eagles have very sharp eyes.
Golden eagles nest on high cliffs.
Diving golden eagles reach over 240 km/h.
ask: Spread your wings like an eagle!
twin: bald-eagle
Golden eagles are all brown; bald eagles have a white head.

photos.by: Richard Bartz, Munich aka Makro Freak

facts: Woodpeckers knock on trees.
They drum to say "this is my tree".
A woodpecker pecks up to 20 times a second.
ask: Drum on the table like a woodpecker!

facts: Swallows have a forked tail.
Swallows catch bugs while flying.
European swallows fly 10,000 km to South Africa every autumn.
ask: Zoom around like a swallow!

facts: Cuckoos say their name: cuck-oo!
Cuckoos lay eggs in other birds' nests.
Young cuckoos fly to Africa alone, never having seen the way.
ask: Say cuck-oo like a cuckoo clock!

facts: Puffins have colourful beaks.
Puffins hold many fish at once.
A puffin once carried 62 little fish in its beak.
ask: How many fish could you hold?

facts: Seagulls live by the sea.
Seagulls stomp to bring worms up.
Chicks peck the red spot on the parent's beak to ask for food.
ask: Stomp like a seagull calling worms!

facts: Flamingos are pink.
Their food makes them pink.
Flamingos eat with their heads upside down.
ask: Stand on one leg like a flamingo — how long?

facts: Bees make honey.
Bees dance to show friends where flowers are.
One jar of honey needs bees to visit about 2 million flowers.
ask: Do a waggle dance like a bee!
twin: wasp
Bees are fuzzy and brown-gold; wasps are smooth and bright yellow-black.

facts: Bumblebees are big and fluffy.
Bumblebees shiver to keep warm.
Bumblebees shake flowers with a buzz to free the pollen.
ask: Buzz like a bumblebee!

facts: Wasps are yellow and black.
Wasps chew wood to make paper nests.
Wasps were making paper long before people were.
ask: Stay calm and still if a wasp comes!

facts: Ladybirds are red with black spots.
This ladybird has seven spots.
One ladybird eats around 5,000 aphids in its life.
ask: Count the spots: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7!

facts: It has big eyes on its wings.
The eyes scare birds away.
It rubs its wings to make a hiss you can hear.
ask: Flap your arms like butterfly wings!

facts: It has big jaws like antlers.
Males wrestle with their jaws.
Stag beetle babies live in old wood for up to 6 years.
ask: Show your strongest pinch!

facts: Snails carry their house.
Snails have eyes on their tentacles.
A snail has thousands of tiny teeth on its tongue.
ask: Move as slowly as a snail!

facts: Spiders have eight legs.
Spiders spin sticky webs.
This spider builds a new web almost every day.
ask: Count to eight on your fingers!

facts: Frogs jump and croak.
Tadpoles turn into frogs.
Frogs drink water through their skin.
ask: Jump like a frog!
twin: common-toad
Frogs have smooth wet skin and long legs; toads are bumpy and walk.

photos.by: Richard Bartz, Munich aka Makro Freak Image:MFB.jpg

facts: Toads are bumpy.
Toads walk more than they jump.
Toads return to the pond where they were born to lay eggs.
ask: Crawl like a toad!

facts: It is black with yellow spots.
Bright colours say "don't eat me".
Fire salamanders can live for more than 20 years.
ask: Find something yellow and black!

facts: Lizards love sunshine.
Lizards warm up on sunny rocks.
A lizard can drop its tail to escape and grow a new one.
ask: Lie in the sun like a lizard!

facts: Snakes have no legs.
Grass snakes are great swimmers.
When scared, it pretends to be dead.
ask: Wiggle like a snake!

facts: Lions roar very loudly.
Lions live in families called prides.
A lion's roar can be heard 8 km away.
ask: Roar like a lion — quietly, then LOUD!
twin: tiger
Lions are golden and plain; tigers are orange with black stripes.

facts: Elephants have a long trunk.
Elephants drink by sucking water into their trunk.
Elephants talk with rumbles too deep for us to hear.
ask: Make a trunk with your arm and trumpet!
twin: asian-elephant
African elephants have huge ears shaped like Africa; Asian elephants have smaller rounded ears.

facts: Giraffes have very long necks.
A giraffe's tongue is dark blue-purple.
A giraffe neck has seven bones — the same number as yours.
ask: Stretch your neck as tall as a giraffe!

sound.by: Anton Baotic, Florian Sicks and Angela S. Stoeger

facts: Zebras have black and white stripes.
No two zebras have the same stripes.
Stripes help keep biting flies away.
ask: Draw stripes on paper like a zebra!
twin: horse
Zebras are striped and wild; horses are one colour and live with people.

facts: Hippos love the water.
Hippos can't really swim — they bounce along the bottom.
Hippo skin makes a red liquid that works like sunscreen.
ask: Open your mouth wide like a hippo!

facts: Cheetahs are the fastest runners.
Cheetahs chirp like birds.
A cheetah goes from 0 to 100 km/h in about 3 seconds.
ask: Run on the spot as fast as a cheetah!
twin: leopard
Cheetahs have round spots and black tear lines; leopards have rosettes like flowers.

sound.by: Smirnova D, Volodin I, Demina T, Volodina E

facts: Leopards climb trees.
Leopards carry food up into trees.
A leopard can haul an animal heavier than itself up a tree.
ask: Climb like a leopard over the sofa!
twin: jaguar
Jaguars are chunkier, with dots inside their rosettes; leopards have empty rosettes.

facts: Hyenas sound like they are laughing.
Mummy hyenas are the bosses.
Hyenas can crunch and eat bones.
ask: Make your silliest laugh!

facts: Chimps hug and tickle.
Chimps use sticks to fish for termites.
Chimps share almost 99% of their DNA with us.
ask: Give someone a chimp hug!
twin: orangutan
Chimps are black and live in Africa; orangutans are orange and live in Asia.

facts: Gorillas beat their chests.
Gorillas build a new bed every night.
Gorillas are mostly vegetarian, yet super strong.
ask: Pat your chest like a gorilla!

facts: Meerkats stand on their back legs.
One meerkat keeps watch for danger.
Meerkats teach their babies how to eat scorpions safely.
ask: Stand tall and look around like a meerkat!

facts: Warthogs run with their tails up.
Warthogs kneel down to eat grass.
Warthogs back into burrows so their tusks face out.
ask: Run with your arm up like a warthog tail!

facts: Crocodiles have lots of teeth.
Baby crocs call from inside the egg.
Crocodiles have lived on Earth since the dinosaurs.
ask: Snap your arms like crocodile jaws!
twin: alligator
Crocodiles have a pointy V snout and show their teeth; alligators have a round U snout.

facts: Ostriches can't fly, but run fast.
Ostrich eggs are the biggest eggs.
One ostrich egg is as big as about 24 chicken eggs.
ask: Run with long ostrich steps!
twin: emu
Ostriches have two toes and bare necks; emus have three toes and shaggy grey-brown feathers.

facts: Some penguins live where it is warm.
They bray like donkeys.
Each one has its own pattern of black spots on its chest.
ask: Waddle like a penguin!
twin: magellanic-penguin
African penguins have one black chest band; Magellanic penguins have two.

facts: Lemurs have stripy tails.
Lemurs sunbathe with arms open.
Lemurs live only on the island of Madagascar.
ask: Open your arms to the sun like a lemur!

facts: Rhinos have horns on their nose.
White rhinos are actually grey.
Rhino horn is made of the same stuff as your fingernails.
ask: Touch your fingernail — that is rhino horn stuff!
twin: indian-rhino
White rhinos have two horns; Indian rhinos have one horn and armour-like skin.

facts: Wildebeest walk in huge herds.
Baby wildebeest run minutes after birth.
Over a million wildebeest travel in a giant circle every year.
ask: March like a big herd!

facts: Wild dogs have big round ears.
Each one has a unique patchy coat.
Wild dogs "vote" on when to hunt by sneezing.
ask: Sneeze to vote — achoo!

sound.by: Elsa Sandoval, Stichting Painted Dog Conservation

facts: This camel has one hump.
The hump stores fat, not water.
A thirsty camel can drink 100 litres in 10 minutes.
ask: How many humps: one or two?
twin: bactrian-camel
Dromedaries have ONE hump; Bactrian camels have TWO.

sound.by: J.P Longre. S. Mercier. M.Harry. P. Louisons. C. Ferry. G. Muys. K. Lens. B. Picard. V. Sandrilli. H. Van Hoeven. L. Rodriguez. B. Couderc

facts: Grey parrots can talk.
They have a bright red tail.
One grey parrot, Alex, learned over 100 words and colours.
ask: Teach a parrot word: what would it be?

facts: It has long legs and feathers on its head.
It stomps on snakes.
Its kick is five times its own body weight in force.
ask: Stomp your feet fast!

facts: Its beak looks like a big shoe.
It stands very still for ages.
Shoebills clatter their beaks like a machine gun to say hello.
ask: Find a shoe — is it as big as a shoebill beak?

facts: Chameleons change colour.
Each eye looks a different way.
Its tongue shoots out faster than you can blink.
ask: Look left and right at the same time!

facts: Dung beetles roll balls of poo.
They roll in a straight line.
Some steer at night by looking at the Milky Way.
ask: Roll a ball in a straight line!

facts: Tigers have orange fur and black stripes.
Tigers love to swim.
Tiger skin is striped too, not just the fur.
ask: Prowl like a tiger on all fours!

photos.by: Photo (c)2007 Derek and Julie Ramsey (Ram-Man) edit by Chris_huh.

facts: Pandas are black and white bears.
Pandas eat bamboo almost all day.
A panda has a "thumb" — a special wrist bone for holding bamboo.
ask: Pretend to munch bamboo like a panda!
twin: red-panda
Giant pandas are big black-and-white bears; red pandas are small, red and fluffy.

facts: Red pandas have a stripy fluffy tail.
They wrap their tail around them like a blanket.
They were called "panda" first — before the giant panda.
ask: Wrap up in a blanket like a red panda tail!

photos.by: Christian Mehlführer, User:Chmehl. Edit by Böhringer
Original: Ganga Raj Sunuwar Derivative work: UnpetitproleX

sound.by: No machine-readable author provided. Mizunoryu assumed (based on copyright claims).

facts: Elephants love bath time.
Elephants remember friends for years.
Elephants comfort upset friends with gentle trunk touches.
ask: Spray pretend water like an elephant!

facts: Orangutans have orange hair.
Orangutans use leaves as umbrellas.
Their name means "person of the forest".
ask: Hold a leaf umbrella over your head!

sound.by: Lameira A, Hardus M, Bartlett A, Shumaker R, Wich S, Menken S

facts: Snow leopards live in snowy mountains.
They wrap their thick tail round their face.
Snow leopards can't roar — they "chuff" instead.
ask: Cover your nose with your scarf like a tail!

photos.by: Original: Tambako The Jaguar Derivative work: User:Niabot

facts: Peacocks open a giant tail fan.
The fan has eyes on it.
Peacocks shake their tail to make a sound we can't hear.
ask: Open your fingers like a peacock fan!

facts: It spreads a hood around its neck.
It is the longest venomous snake.
King cobras mostly eat other snakes.
ask: Make a hood with your hands!

facts: It is the biggest lizard.
It smells with its forked tongue.
Komodo dragons live on just a few islands in Indonesia.
ask: Flick your tongue to "smell"!
twin: water-monitor
Komodo dragons are bigger and live on a few islands; water monitors swim in cities like Singapore.

facts: Sun bears have a sun on their chest.
They have a very long tongue for honey.
Sun bears are the smallest bears in the world.
ask: Draw a sun on paper!

facts: Snow monkeys take hot baths.
They have red faces.
Some snow monkeys make snowballs just to play.
ask: What would you build with snow?

sound.by: Furuyama T, Kobayasi K, Riquimaroux H

facts: Cranes dance and jump.
Pairs sing together.
In Japan, cranes mean long life and good luck.
ask: Dance a crane dance with someone!

facts: This camel has two humps.
Thick winter fur falls off in spring.
Bactrian camels can eat snow for water.
ask: Make two humps with your knees!

facts: This rhino has one horn.
Its skin looks like armour plates.
Indian rhinos are good swimmers.
ask: How many horns: one or two?

facts: Tapirs are black and white.
Tapirs have a tiny trunk.
Baby tapirs have stripes and spots like watermelons.
ask: Wiggle your nose like a tapir trunk!

facts: This monkey has a big nose.
They swim with webbed feet.
A big nose makes their honking calls louder.
ask: Honk like a proboscis monkey!

facts: Otters live in families.
Singapore otter families swim right through the city.
Otter families "talk" with over a dozen different calls.
ask: How many people are in your family "romp"?

facts: Its tail is longer than its body.
It loves crabs and fruit.
Some macaques use stones to crack shells.
ask: Never feed monkeys — why do you think?

facts: It has an orange tummy.
It runs along wires and trees.
It loves bananas — plantain is a kind of banana.
ask: Spot a squirrel on a tree outside!

facts: Hornbills have a big horn on the beak.
Daddy feeds mummy through a slit in the nest.
Mummy seals herself into a tree hole to keep the eggs safe.
ask: Pass a snack through a tiny gap!

facts: Koels sing "ko-el" very loudly.
Daddy is black with red eyes.
Koels lay their eggs in crows' nests.
ask: Call "ko-EL" like the morning bird!

facts: Mynas walk instead of hop.
They have yellow beaks and feet.
Thousands sleep together in one tree at night.
ask: Walk, don't hop, like a myna!

photos.by: Lip Kee Yap from Singapore, Republic of Singapore

facts: It is a big lizard that swims.
It can stay underwater for 30 minutes.
It is the second-heaviest lizard in the world.
ask: Hold your breath — 1, 2, 3!

facts: Pangolins are covered in scales.
They roll into a ball like an artichoke.
A pangolin can eat 70 million ants and termites in a year.
ask: Roll up small like a pangolin!

photos.by: Piekfrosch at German Wikipedia (Original text: Piekfrosch (Wikipedia-User))

facts: Colugos glide between trees.
Its skin is like a kite.
A colugo can glide over 100 metres in one go.
ask: Spread your arms and glide!

facts: Daddy has bright orange "sails".
They nest high up in trees.
Ducklings jump from the tree nest and bounce safely.
ask: How many colours can you see?
twin: mallard
Mandarin drakes are orange and colourful; mallard drakes have a green head.

facts: It is a huge moth.
Its wing tips look like snake heads.
Grown-up atlas moths have no mouth and never eat.
ask: Is it bigger than your hand?

facts: Black bears climb trees.
Some black bears are brown or even white.
Black bears can open car doors to look for food.
ask: Climb like a bear up the stairs!

facts: Bison have a big furry hump.
Bison roll in dust to clean.
Bison can run 55 km/h and jump 2 metres high.
ask: Roll on the floor like a bison!

facts: Raccoons wear a black mask.
Raccoons feel food with clever hands.
Raccoons remember how to solve puzzles for 3 years.
ask: Feel something with eyes closed — what is it?

facts: Beavers slap their tail on water.
Beavers build dams across rivers.
One beaver dam in Canada is so big you can see it from space.
ask: Slap your hand like a beaver tail!

facts: It lifts its white tail like a flag.
The flag says "danger, run!"
White-tailed deer can jump higher than a grown-up.
ask: Wave a white flag like a deer tail!

facts: Coyotes yip and howl.
Coyotes live even in big cities.
Coyotes sometimes hunt together with badgers.
ask: Yip and howl like a coyote!

facts: Skunks are black with a white stripe.
They spray a stinky smell.
Skunks stamp their feet as a warning first.
ask: Hold your nose — pee-yew!

facts: Opossum babies ride on mummy's back.
Opossums "play dead" when scared.
It is the only animal with a pouch north of Mexico.
ask: Carry a toy on your back like an opossum!

video.by: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service - Midwest Region

facts: Bald eagles have white heads.
They are not bald — the white is feathers.
Their nests can weigh as much as a car.
ask: Soar like an eagle around the room!

photos.by: Haliaeetus_leucocephalus_LC0195.jpg: Jörg Hempel derivative work: Samwb123 (talk)

facts: It has an orange-red tummy.
It pulls worms from the lawn.
Settlers named it after the robin back home in Europe.
ask: Look for worms after the rain!

facts: Daddy cardinal is bright red.
Cardinals sing all year.
Daddy feeds mummy seeds, beak to beak.
ask: Find something red near you!

facts: Blue jays are bright blue.
They copy the scream of hawks.
Blue jays plant oak forests by burying acorns.
ask: Hide something and find it later!

facts: Geese honk loudly.
They fly in a V shape.
Flying in a V saves energy — they take turns at the front.
ask: Make a V with your arms and fly!

facts: Hummingbirds are tiny.
Their wings hum as they fly.
They can fly backwards — the only birds that can.
ask: Walk backwards like a hummingbird flies!

facts: Alligators have a round snout.
Mummy carries babies in her mouth.
Nest warmth decides if babies are boys or girls.
ask: Make a U shape with your hands!

facts: Monarchs are orange and black.
They fly to Mexico for winter.
The trip is so long it takes great-grandchildren to come back.
ask: Fly to a far-away place in the room!

facts: Grey squirrels are great jumpers.
They pretend to bury nuts to trick thieves.
They were brought to Britain and Italy from America.
ask: Pretend to hide a nut — trick someone!

facts: Polar bears live on the ice.
Polar bear skin is black under white fur.
Polar bears can swim for days without stopping.
ask: Slide on your tummy like a polar bear!

facts: Arctic foxes turn white in winter.
They have furry feet.
Their fur is so warm they only shiver at minus 70 °C.
ask: What do you wear to stay warm?

facts: Sea otters float on their backs.
They hold hands while they sleep.
Sea otters use a rock on their tummy to crack shells.
ask: Hold hands like sleeping sea otters!

photos.by: Mike Baird from Morro Bay, USA (bairdphotos.com)
Mike Baird from Morro Bay, USA

facts: Prairie dogs live in towns underground.
They greet each other with a kiss.
Their calls describe what a visitor looks like.
ask: Describe someone with sounds only!

video.by: No machine-readable author provided. W0lfie assumed (based on copyright claims).

facts: It has feather tufts like horns.
Its eyes are big and yellow.
Its grip is strong enough to carry a skunk.
ask: Make owl eyes with your fingers!

video.by: Bureau of Land Management Oregon and Washington

facts: Jaguars have spotted coats.
Jaguars love to swim.
For its size, a jaguar has the strongest bite of any big cat.
ask: Pretend to swim like a jaguar!

facts: Capybaras are giant guinea pigs.
Birds ride on their backs.
It is the biggest rodent in the world.
ask: Sit calmly like a capybara!

facts: Anteaters have a long nose.
They have no teeth at all.
Its tongue flicks 150 times a minute.
ask: Stick your tongue out fast!

facts: Sloths move very slowly.
Sloths hang upside down.
Green algae grow in sloth fur.
ask: Move slow-slow-slow like a sloth!

facts: Macaws are red, yellow and blue.
They eat clay to settle their tummies.
Macaws pair up for life and fly wing to wing.
ask: Name the colours: red, yellow, blue!

facts: Toucans have huge colourful beaks.
The beak is light and hollow.
The beak works like a radiator to cool the bird.
ask: Make a big beak with your hands!

facts: Anacondas are giant snakes.
They live in rivers and swamps.
It is the heaviest snake in the world.
ask: Stretch out long like an anaconda!

facts: Llamas hum to each other.
Llamas carry bags in the mountains.
Llamas guard sheep from coyotes.
ask: Hum like a llama!

facts: Giant tortoises are very slow.
They can live over 100 years.
The Galápagos islands are named after these tortoises.
ask: How old would you be in 100 years?

facts: It is tiny and bright red.
Bright colours mean "don't touch!"
Mummy carries each tadpole up a tree to its own pool.
ask: Look, don't touch — practise with a toy!

facts: It has big red eyes.
It sleeps on leaves all day.
It flashes its red eyes to startle hungry snakes.
ask: Open your eyes wide — surprise!

facts: Howler monkeys are very loud.
They howl every morning.
You can hear them almost 5 km away.
ask: Howl a morning song!

facts: Condors have giant wings.
They glide for hours without flapping.
One condor flew over 170 km without flapping its wings once.
ask: Glide with arms wide without flapping!

facts: Giant otters are as long as a grown-up.
They live in big families.
Each one has a unique white throat pattern.
ask: Look at your fingerprints — all different!

facts: These penguins live in South America.
They come back to the same burrow every year.
They swim thousands of kilometres north each winter.
ask: Find your way back to your bed!

sound.by: Christoph Moning, alguns direitos reservados (CC BY)

facts: Iguanas are green lizards.
They jump into rivers from trees.
Iguanas have a third "eye" on top of their head.
ask: Can you find your eyes, nose and ears?

facts: Armadillos wear armour.
They can hold their breath for 6 minutes.
They walk underwater across streams.
ask: Hold your breath and count!

facts: Its wings are shiny blue.
The underside is brown, like a dead leaf.
The blue is not paint — it is tiny scales that bend light.
ask: Find something shiny!

facts: Kangaroos hop on big feet.
Baby kangaroos live in a pouch.
A newborn joey is the size of a jelly bean.
ask: Hop like a kangaroo — how far can you go?

facts: Koalas hug trees.
Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day.
Koalas have fingerprints almost like ours.
ask: Hug a tree — or a grown-up!

video.by: Charlton B, Ellis W, McKinnon A, Brumm J, Nilsson K, Fitch W

facts: A platypus has a duck bill.
It is a mammal that lays eggs.
Its fur glows blue-green under UV light.
ask: Which animals is a platypus a mix of?

facts: Echidnas are spiky.
Echidnas lay eggs.
A baby echidna is called a puggle.
ask: Say "puggle" three times fast!

facts: Wombats dig big burrows.
Their pouch faces backwards.
Wombats make cube-shaped poo.
ask: Draw a cube — like wombat poo!

facts: Kookaburras sound like laughing.
They laugh together at sunrise.
Kookaburras are giant kingfishers that don't fish much.
ask: Laugh like a kookaburra!
twin: kingfisher
Both are kingfishers! The kookaburra is big and brown; the common kingfisher is tiny and blue.

facts: Emus can't fly.
Daddy emus sit on the eggs.
Emus can run 50 km/h on long legs.
ask: Run with big emu strides!

facts: Devils make spooky screeches.
Their ears turn red when upset.
They live only on the island of Tasmania.
ask: Make a spooky screech!

facts: Cockatoos have a yellow crest.
They raise the crest when excited.
Sydney cockatoos learned to open wheelie bins.
ask: Put your hands up like a crest!

facts: Kiwis can't fly.
Kiwis have nostrils at the tip of their beak.
A kiwi egg is huge — 20% of mummy's weight.
ask: Sniff like a kiwi looking for worms!

facts: It is the biggest reptile.
It swims in rivers and the sea.
Salties can surf ocean currents between islands.
ask: Float still like a log!

facts: Quokkas look like they are smiling.
Quokkas hop like small kangaroos.
Rottnest Island was named "rat nest" after them.
ask: Show your best quokka smile!

facts: It has all the rainbow colours.
It drinks nectar with a brush tongue.
Lorikeets play by hanging upside down and rolling.
ask: Name all the colours of a rainbow!

facts: It opens a big frill around its neck.
It runs on two legs.
The frill pops open like an umbrella to look scary.
ask: Make a big frill with your hands!

facts: Keas are mountain parrots.
Keas love to play in snow.
Keas are so curious they pull rubber off cars.
ask: What would a curious kea do in your room?

facts: Buffalo have big curly horns.
They live in herds of hundreds.
A herd "votes" where to go by standing and facing that way.
ask: Face the same way as everyone — vote like a buffalo herd!

facts: An okapi has zebra stripes on its legs.
It is the giraffe’s only living cousin.
Its tongue is so long it can lick its own ears.
ask: Can you touch your nose with your tongue?
twin: zebra
Okapis only have stripes on their legs and are brown; zebras are striped all over.

facts: Fennec foxes have giant ears.
Big ears let heat out in the hot desert.
Fur on their feet stops them burning on hot sand.
ask: Cup your hands behind your ears — can you hear better?
twin: red-fox
Fennec foxes are tiny and sandy with huge ears; red foxes are bigger and orange.

facts: Baboons live in big troops.
Babies ride on mummy’s back.
Baboons groom each other to stay friends.
ask: Give someone a gentle back scratch, baboon style!

facts: A mandrill has a red and blue face.
It keeps food in its cheek pouches.
It is the most colourful monkey in the world.
ask: Puff your cheeks full like a mandrill!

facts: It wears a golden crown of feathers.
Cranes dance and jump to say hello.
It is the national bird of Uganda.
ask: Dance a crane dance with jumps!

facts: Aardvark means "earth pig".
It digs super fast with strong claws.
Its old burrows become homes for many other animals.
ask: Say "aardvark" — it’s one of the first words in the dictionary!

facts: An oryx has long straight horns.
It lives in deserts.
It can go for weeks without drinking water.
ask: Make long horns with your arms!

facts: Vultures have bald heads.
They clean up the land by eating leftovers.
Vultures can soar for hours without flapping.
ask: Why might a bald head help keep clean?

facts: Rheas can’t fly but run fast.
Daddy rheas look after the eggs.
One nest can hold 50 eggs from many mummies.
ask: Count to 50 like the eggs in a rhea nest!
twin: ostrich
Rheas are smaller and grey-brown with three toes; ostriches are bigger with two toes.

facts: Vicuñas live high in the mountains.
They have the softest wool.
They are the wild cousins of alpacas.
ask: Feel something soft — what is it?
twin: llama
Vicuñas are small, wild and golden; llamas are big, tame and many colours.

facts: It has rings round its eyes like glasses.
It is the only bear in South America.
It builds a nest in trees to rest.
ask: Make glasses with your fingers!

facts: It is a tiny golden monkey.
It has a mane like a lion.
Daddy and big brothers carry the babies.
ask: Who carries you when you’re tired?

facts: Caimans are small crocodile cousins.
Their eyes glow red at night.
Thousands live together in the Pantanal wetland.
ask: Peek like a caiman with just your eyes!

facts: Coatis have a long stripy tail.
They hold their tails up high.
Their wiggly nose sniffs out bugs under leaves.
ask: Walk with your arm up like a coati tail!

facts: It looks like a fox on stilts.
Its long legs see over tall grass.
It loves eating a fruit called "wolf apple".
ask: Walk on your tiptoes like a maned wolf!

facts: It has a crown of grey feathers.
Its claws are as big as bear claws.
It catches monkeys and sloths in the treetops.
ask: Show your biggest claws!

facts: It has a spiky punk hairdo.
Chicks have claws on their wings.
It smells like cow poo — people call it the stinkbird!
ask: Hold your nose — pee-yew!

facts: It has a helmet on its head.
It has blue and red skin on its neck.
It plants rainforest trees by spreading seeds.
ask: Plant a seed and watch it grow!
twin: emu
Cassowaries are black with a helmet and blue neck; emus are brown and shaggy.

facts: This kangaroo lives in trees!
It can jump down from 15 metres.
Its tail helps it balance on branches.
ask: Balance on a line like a tree kangaroo!
twin: red-kangaroo
Tree kangaroos are small, dark and climb trees; red kangaroos are big and hop across deserts.

facts: Sugar gliders glide between trees.
They love sweet tree sap.
They can glide as far as half a football pitch.
ask: Spread your arms and glide across the room!
twin: colugo
Sugar gliders are tiny with big eyes; colugos are bigger with a kite of skin to their tail.

facts: It is the smallest penguin.
It is blue, not black.
At sunset they parade up the beach to their burrows.
ask: Waddle in a sunset parade!

facts: Wallabies are small kangaroos.
Babies are called joeys too.
Wallabies thump the ground to warn friends.
ask: Hop small, then hop big!
twin: red-kangaroo
Wallabies are small like a dog; red kangaroos are as tall as a grown-up.

facts: It is a parrot that can’t fly.
It smells sweet like honey.
Every kākāpō in the world has its own name.
ask: What name would you give a kākāpō?

facts: Yaks have long shaggy hair.
They live on the roof of the world.
Yaks grunt instead of saying moo.
ask: Grunt like a yak instead of mooing!
twin: bison
Yaks have long hair to the ground; bison have a big woolly hump.

facts: Gibbons swing through trees.
Families sing together every morning.
Gibbons swing as fast as a car in town.
ask: Sing a morning song with your family!
twin: orangutan
Gibbons are small and slim with very long arms; orangutans are big, heavy and orange.

facts: Sloth bears have shaggy black fur.
They suck up termites like a vacuum.
Mummy carries the cubs on her back.
ask: Slurp like a vacuum cleaner!

facts: Tarsiers have huge eyes.
Each eye is as big as its brain.
They can turn their head almost all the way round.
ask: Make your eyes as big as you can!

facts: A gharial has a very thin snout.
The thin snout is perfect for catching fish.
Males have a bump on the nose like a pot.
ask: Make a long thin snout with your hands!
twin: nile-crocodile
Gharials have a long skinny snout; crocodiles have a wide one.

facts: Mongooses are fast and brave.
They can fight snakes.
Their quickness helps them dodge a cobra’s bite.
ask: How fast can you dodge?

facts: Slow lorises move very slowly.
They have huge night eyes.
They are wild animals — never pets.
ask: Move in slow motion like a loris!

photos.by: Lucie Čižmářová, The Kukang Rescue Program

facts: Cougars are big cats that can’t roar.
They purr like house cats.
Cougars live from Canada all the way to Chile.
ask: Purr like a giant cat!
twin: lynx
Cougars are big with a long tail; lynx are smaller with a short tail and ear tufts.

video.by: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, National Conservation Training Center (USFWS/NCTC)

facts: Daddy elk have huge antlers.
In autumn they "bugle" with a high whistle.
One bugle can be heard over a kilometre away.
ask: Whistle a high elk bugle!
twin: moose
Elk have pointy antlers and a pale bottom; moose have flat antlers and a long nose.

facts: Pronghorns are super fast runners.
They can run 90 km/h.
Scientists think they got so fast running from cheetahs that lived in America long ago.
ask: Run fast like a pronghorn — on the spot!

facts: Turkeys say gobble gobble.
Wild turkeys can fly.
Their heads change colour when excited.
ask: Gobble like a turkey!

facts: Manatees are gentle sea cows.
They eat lots of sea grass.
Manatees are cousins of elephants.
ask: Float slowly like a manatee!

photos.by: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Headquarters

facts: Chipmunks have stripes on their backs.
They stuff food in their cheeks.
It stores enough food in its burrow for the whole winter.
ask: Pretend to stuff nuts in your cheeks!

facts: Roadrunners prefer running to flying.
They run 30 km/h.
They can catch and eat rattlesnakes.
ask: Run zig-zag like a roadrunner!

facts: It rattles its tail as a warning.
The rattle grows a new piece every time it sheds skin.
It finds warm animals by feeling their heat.
ask: If you hear a rattle, walk away slowly!

facts: Chamois climb steep mountains.
Their horns curl back like hooks.
They can leap 6 metres from rock to rock.
ask: Jump from cushion to cushion!
twin: ibex
Chamois are small with hooked horns; ibex are bigger with long curved horns.

facts: It is one of the biggest owls.
It has orange eyes and ear tufts.
Its deep hoot carries for kilometres at night.
ask: Hoot as deep as you can!
twin: tawny-owl
Eagle owls are huge with orange eyes and ear tufts; tawny owls are smaller with dark eyes.

facts: Ospreys dive feet-first for fish.
They carry fish head-first, like a torpedo.
Ospreys live on every continent except Antarctica.
ask: Point your feet and dive!

facts: Fallow deer have white spots.
Daddies have flat, hand-shaped antlers.
They "pronk" — bounce on all four legs at once.
ask: Bounce on both feet like a pronking deer!
twin: red-deer
Fallow deer are spotted with flat antlers; red deer are bigger with pointy antlers.

facts: A dormouse is a tiny golden mouse.
It sleeps for up to 7 months.
Its name comes from the French word dormir, “to sleep”.
ask: Curl up into a tiny sleepy ball!

photos.by: Björn Schulz (= User Bjoernschulz on de.wikipedia)

facts: Adders have a zig-zag on their back.
They warm up in the morning sun.
Adders live further north than any other snake.
ask: Draw a zig-zag line!
twin: grass-snake
Adders have a zig-zag pattern; grass snakes have a yellow collar.

facts: Stoats have a black tail tip.
Some turn white in winter.
They do a wild "war dance" to confuse rabbits.
ask: Do a silly wiggly dance!

facts: This dolphin is pink!
It lives in rivers, not the sea.
It can turn its neck to swim between flooded trees.
ask: Turn your head like a river dolphin — sea dolphins can’t!
twin: dolphin
River dolphins are pink with a long beak and live in rivers; sea dolphins are grey and live in the ocean.

facts: Ocelots have spots and stripes.
They hunt at night.
Ocelots are great swimmers, unlike most cats.
ask: Draw spots and stripes together!
twin: jaguar
Ocelots are small like a dog; jaguars are big and heavy.

facts: Spider monkeys have long arms and legs.
Their tail can hold on like a hand.
They can hang from a branch by just their tail.
ask: Make your arms long like a spider monkey!

facts: Squirrel monkeys are small and yellow.
They live in big noisy groups.
A group can have more than 100 monkeys.
ask: How many friends are in your group?

photos.by: Mike's Birds from Riverside, CA, US

facts: Guanacos are wild llamas.
They live in mountains and dry plains.
Their thick blood helps them breathe high in the mountains.
ask: Breathe slowly like you are high on a mountain!
twin: llama
Guanacos are wild and brown with a grey face; llamas are tame and come in many colours.

facts: It is a big blue parrot.
It has yellow rings around its eyes.
Its beak is strong enough to crack coconuts.
ask: Find something blue and something yellow!
twin: scarlet-macaw
Hyacinth macaws are all blue; scarlet macaws are red, yellow and blue.

facts: Dingoes are Australia’s wild dogs.
Dingoes howl but rarely bark.
Dingoes can turn their heads almost all the way round.
ask: Howl like a dingo — no barking!
twin: dog
Dingoes are wild and sandy-coloured; pet dogs live with people and come in all colours.

facts: It has a tail shaped like a diamond.
It is Australia’s biggest bird of prey.
It can soar higher than 1,800 metres.
ask: Make a diamond with your fingers!

facts: It has a bright blue tongue.
It sticks its tongue out to scare enemies.
Mummy has live babies instead of laying eggs.
ask: Stick out your tongue — is it blue?

facts: It looks like a lizard but isn’t one.
It has spikes along its back.
Its family is older than the dinosaurs.
ask: Can you name something older than dinosaurs?

facts: Gazelles have a black stripe on their side.
They jump high when they run away.
They wag their tails all the time.
ask: Jump high like a gazelle!

facts: Pelicans have a big pouch under their beak.
They fish together in a circle.
The pouch can hold more than a bucket of water.
ask: Scoop like a pelican with your hands!

facts: Impalas can jump very far.
Daddies have curly horns.
An impala can leap 10 metres in one jump.
ask: How far can you jump?
twin: gazelle
Impalas are bigger and red-brown with an M on their bottom; gazelles have a black side stripe.

facts: Lovebirds are small colourful parrots.
Pairs sit close together.
They carry nest material tucked in their feathers.
ask: Sit close to someone you love!

facts: Dolphins jump and play.
Dolphins breathe air through a blowhole.
Each dolphin has its own whistle, like a name.
ask: Make up a whistle name for yourself!
twin: orca
Dolphins are grey; orcas are big black-and-white dolphins.

facts: Whales sing long songs.
Humpbacks jump right out of the water.
Humpbacks swim 8,000 km between feeding and baby seas.
ask: Sing a long whale song!
twin: blue-whale
Humpbacks have long white flippers; blue whales are much longer and blue-grey.

sound.by: Garland E, Gedamke J, Rekdahl M, Noad M, Garrigue C, Gales N

facts: It is the biggest animal ever.
It eats tiny shrimp called krill.
Its heart is as heavy as two grown-ups.
ask: What is the biggest thing you can see?

facts: Orcas are black and white.
Orcas are actually big dolphins.
Grandma orcas lead the family to food.
ask: Who leads your family on walks?

facts: Sea turtles swim with flippers.
Baby turtles race from the beach to the sea.
Mummy turtles come back to the beach where they hatched.
ask: Paddle your arms like flippers!

facts: Seals rest on beaches.
Seals have whiskers that feel fish moving.
Seals can sleep underwater and float up to breathe.
ask: Wiggle on your tummy like a seal!

facts: Walruses have long tusks.
They use tusks to climb onto ice.
Walruses can sleep while floating, using air pouches like a pillow.
ask: Make tusks with two fingers!

facts: Emperor penguins live in Antarctica.
Daddy keeps the egg warm on his feet.
Thousands huddle and take turns in the warm middle.
ask: Huddle together like penguins!

facts: It wears a white ring around each eye.
It builds its nest out of pebbles.
Some steal pebbles from their neighbours’ nests!
ask: Collect five pebbles — build a nest!
twin: emperor-penguin
Adélie penguins are small with white eye rings; emperors are big with yellow-orange ears.

facts: King penguins have orange patches.
Chicks are brown and fluffy like teddy bears.
Parents find their chick among thousands by its voice.
ask: Call your name — can someone find you with eyes closed?
twin: emperor-penguin
King penguins are a bit smaller with bright orange "ears"; emperors are bigger and live on the ice.

facts: It has spots like a leopard.
It has a big smiley mouth.
Underwater, leopard seals sing long trilling songs.
ask: Make a big smile like a leopard seal!
twin: harbour-seal
Leopard seals are huge with a long head and big mouth; harbour seals are small and round.

facts: It has the longest wings of any bird.
It can glide for hours without flapping.
Young albatrosses stay out at sea for years before they land again.
ask: Spread your arms as wide as you can — an albatross is even wider!

facts: It lives further south than any other mammal.
It saws breathing holes in the ice with its teeth.
It can stay underwater for over an hour.
ask: How long can you hold your breath? A Weddell seal can do an hour!

facts: Dogs wag their tails when happy.
Dogs smell 10,000 times better than us.
Dogs understand when you point — most animals don't.
ask: Point at something — does a dog get it?

facts: Cats purr when they are happy.
Cats see well in the dark.
Grown-up cats meow mostly to talk to people.
ask: Purr like a happy cat!

facts: Cows say moo.
Cows have best friends.
Cows chew their food twice.
ask: Moo like a cow!

facts: Horses gallop fast.
Horses can sleep standing up.
Horses have the biggest eyes of any land mammal.
ask: Gallop around the room!

sound.by: Lemasson A, Remeuf K, Trabalon M, Cuir F, Hausberger M

facts: Pigs say oink.
Pigs roll in mud to stay cool.
Pigs are as clever as dogs — maybe cleverer!
ask: Oink like a pig!

facts: Sheep have woolly coats.
Wool keeps sheep warm and dry.
Sheep remember 50 sheep faces for years.
ask: Baa like a sheep!

facts: Goats love to climb.
Goats have square pupils.
Goats have accents — their bleats change with friends.
ask: Climb onto a cushion like a goat!

facts: Chickens lay eggs.
Roosters crow cock-a-doodle-doo.
Chickens are living cousins of T. rex!
ask: Crow like a rooster!

facts: Donkeys say hee-haw.
Donkeys have very long ears.
A donkey's bray can be heard 3 km away.
ask: Hee-haw like a donkey!
twin: horse
Donkeys are smaller with very long ears; horses have short ears and long manes.
